# FastAPI-Restly

> FastAPI-Restly (`fr`) is a REST framework for FastAPI, using SQLAlchemy 2.0 and Pydantic v2, with class-based views that support full customization through inheritance and mixins.

The Guide has one page for each part of Restly, in five groups. Each page
starts with how that part works, then shows how to use it. If you are new to
Restly, start with the tutorial, [Build a Blog API](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/tutorial.html).

You write a SQLAlchemy model and a view class, and Restly turns the view into
FastAPI routes. This is what happens when a client sends `PATCH /projects/1`.
FastAPI first checks the request body against the update body,
`ProjectUpdate`:

```
PATCH /projects/1
  └─ update_endpoint(id, schema_obj)      # endpoint method: HTTP contract
       ├─ handle_update(id, schema_obj)   # handler: runs the steps
       │    ├─ get_one(id)                # loads through the scope, or 404
       │    ├─ authorize("update", ...)   # may the caller do this? Or 403
       │    ├─ update(obj, schema_obj)    # business method: the change
       │    ├─ before_action_commit(...)
       │    ├─ commit
       │    └─ after_action_commit(...)
       └─ to_response(obj)                # the response class, as JSON
```

These are the parts, and the page that explains each one:

- **Model**: your SQLAlchemy model, on a declarative base of your own.
  Restly works with it, but does not own it. See [Models](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/models.html).
- **View**: a class that groups related endpoints under a `prefix`.
  `fr.include_view()` registers its
  routes on an app or a router. A CRUD view,
  `fr.AsyncRestView` or
  `fr.RestView`, also names a `model`,
  and serves five routes for it. See [Views](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/views.html) and
  [CRUD Routes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/crud_routes.html).
- **The view's schema**: a Pydantic class that lists the fields of the
  resource. Restly builds the request bodies, such as `ProjectUpdate`, and the
  response class, `ProjectResponse`, from it. A view without a schema gets one
  that Restly generates from the model. See
  [Schemas & Validation](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/schemas.html).
- **Endpoint method, handler and business method**: the three layers of each
  CRUD route. To change what an action does, override the business method,
  such as `update`. To change the HTTP contract, such as the status code,
  replace the endpoint method. A handler is final. See
  [Request Lifecycle & Hooks](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/lifecycle.html).
- **Commit**: a write route commits after the business method.
  `before_action_commit` runs just before the commit, and
  `after_action_commit` just after it. A read does not commit. See
  [What commits, and when](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/lifecycle.html#what-commits).
- **Scope**: the rows of a model that exist for a request. Restly applies it
  to every read of the model and to every reference to the model, so a hidden
  row is a 404. A scope is made of clauses, which are named query rules. See
  [Scopes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/scopes.html) and [Query Clauses](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/clauses.html).
- **`authorize`**: decides whether the caller may do the action. A refusal
  is a 403. See [Authorization](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/authorization.html).
- **`Current`**: the request context. It holds the caller and other values
  for the request. Scopes, column defaults and your `authorize` can read it.
  See [Request Context](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/context.html).
- **List params**: the filter, sort and page parameters of the list route.
  Restly builds them from the response class. See
  [Filtering & Pagination](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/filtering.html).
- **Session**: each request gets a database session from the source that
  `fr.configure()` sets. See
  [Database & Configuration](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/database.html).

## Tutorial

- [Tutorial: Build a Blog API](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/tutorial.html)
- [Tutorial: Add Authors and Drafts](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/tutorial_customizing.html)

## Setup

- [New & Existing Projects](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/projects.html): add Restly to an app that you already have, start a new project with `restly new`, lay out a project as it grows, and serve more than one API version.
- [Database & Configuration](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/database.html): tell Restly where its database is, reuse the engine or sessionmaker that your app already has, use another database on one view, such as a read replica, and open a session outside a request.
- [Models](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/models.html): add Restly's defaults and common columns to your models, and set the values that every write needs, such as the author or a slug.

## Views & Routes

- [Views](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/views.html): the view classes, how to declare routes and register a view, routes that are not CRUD, such as login and webhooks, and how views share behavior through base classes.
- [CRUD Routes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/crud_routes.html): the five default routes, async or sync, how to leave some routes out, and how to serve a child resource under its parent.
- [Request Lifecycle & Hooks](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/lifecycle.html): the steps of a request, which method to override for each change, custom routes, what commits when, several writes in one commit, and the same logic in a script or a worker.
- [React Admin](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/react_admin.html): connect react-admin to a view, the list format and the routes that react-admin expects, to-many id arrays, CORS, and a list that shows no rows.
- [Type Annotations](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/typing.html): type the schema, the methods that you override and your custom routes.

## Requests & Responses

- [Schemas & Validation](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/schemas.html): generate the schema or write it, keep a field out of the requests or the responses, validate input, and use other field names in JSON, such as camelCase.
- [Relationships](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/relationships.html): accept the id of another row, check that the row exists, return related objects, and fix `MissingGreenlet`.
- [Responses](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/responses.html): what each route returns, the list envelope, and how to change the shape of one route or of all routes.
- [Filtering & Pagination](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/filtering.html): the filters, the sort order and the pages that a client can use on a list.
- [Errors](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/errors.html): raise a 404 or a 403, see why a duplicate value gives a 409, and change the error body.
- [OpenAPI](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/openapi.html): the tags, names and operation IDs of the routes, and how to document a custom route.

## Access

- [Request Context](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/context.html): bind the current user in a dependency, a script or a test.
- [Authorization](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/authorization.html): allow or refuse each action, for each caller.
- [Query Clauses](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/clauses.html): name a query rule once, then reuse and combine it.
- [Scopes](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/scopes.html): hide rows from every read, show each user only their own rows, and soft-delete rows.
- [Multi-Tenancy](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/tenancy.html): keep the rows of each tenant apart.

## Testing & Deploying

- [Testing](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/testing.html): set up the test suite, build the test schema, and use the test clients and fixtures.
- [Deploying](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/deploying.html): read the settings from the environment, run the app, set up Alembic and add a health check.

## What FastAPI covers

- [Security](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/security/): OAuth2, API keys and other security schemes. To make the caller available to your views, see [Request Context](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/context.html#current-request-binding).
- [Middleware](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/middleware/).
- [CORS](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/cors/). For a react-admin frontend, see also [CORS for React Admin](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/react_admin.html#react-admin-cors).
- [Background tasks](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/background-tasks/). For work that must still happen after a crash, use an outbox row in a [transaction hook](https://www.fastapi-restly.org/dev/lifecycle.html#after-action-commit-raises).
- [File uploads](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/request-files/).
- [WebSockets](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/websockets/). Declare them on the app or on a router, not on a view.
